moduleTitle: Creating your first codeless test in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Explain how a codeless test is created in Testim by recording actions in the AUT browser.
Describe how Testim's Smart Locators identify elements so tests survive UI changes.
Explain how a recorded test is saved and how its results are viewed after a run.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Recording: the starting point of every test

elements.description: Creating a test starts by navigating to the relevant website inside the Application Under Test (AUT) browser window and recording the series of actions you want tested — clicks, text entry, scrolling, navigation. Testim captures each action as a step.

Each recorded action becomes a step, shown as a box in the test procedure with an icon in its upper-left corner indicating the action type (click, enter text, scroll, etc.). Steps run top-to-bottom in the order they were recorded, and can be reordered, edited, or deleted afterward.

elements.text: 'Codeless' means no scripting is required to produce a working automated test from a recording — but every step remains editable afterward, including adding validations, which is where the later 'editing tests' skills come in.

bulletPoints: Record actions in the AUT browser → each action becomes an editable step.
Codeless: no code needed to get a first working test from a recording.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Smart Locators: why the test doesn't break on every UI change

elements.description: When an element is selected during recording, Testim's algorithm analyzes potentially hundreds of attributes associated with that element and assigns weights to them to uniquely identify it. These weighted attributes are the element's Locators. Smart Locators also learn with each test run — if some attributes change, Testim falls back to other still-valid attributes instead of failing outright.

elements.text: This is the mechanism that lets a test survive normal UI churn (a class name changing, a button being restyled) without needing to be re-recorded every time — it's what makes the tests genuinely maintainable rather than brittle.

bulletPoints: Testim inspects hundreds of attributes per element and weights them to build a Locator.
Smart Locators adapt across runs, reducing false failures from minor UI changes.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Saving a test and viewing results

elements.description: A recorded test is saved into the project's Test Library, where it can be organized into folders, labeled, and re-run at any time — locally, from the editor, from the CLI, or on a schedule.

After a run, Testim reports pass/fail per step and per test, and surfaces the reason a step failed (e.g. element not found, element not visible) so you can diagnose without re-watching a full manual re-run.

bulletPoints: Saved tests live in the Test Library and can be re-run from the editor, CLI, or a schedule.
Results show pass/fail per step, with the failure reason surfaced for quick diagnosis.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming 'codeless' means 'unchangeable'
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating a recorded test as a fixed artifact that must be re-recorded from scratch whenever it needs a change.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Every recorded step remains fully editable afterward — properties, target elements, validations, and step order can all be changed without re-recording the whole test.

examPitfalls.title: Not trusting Smart Locators to survive minor UI changes
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming any DOM or styling change will break a recorded test, and re-recording pre-emptively.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Smart Locators weight many attributes and adapt across runs specifically so small UI changes don't require a full re-record — use Improve on the target element if a locator genuinely needs refreshing (see the 'How to edit tests' module).

practiceQuiz.scenario: How does Testim create a codeless test?

options.text: By writing Selenium scripts behind the scenes that the user must review.
By recording the series of actions taken in the AUT browser and turning each into an editable step.
By importing a manual test case document and converting it automatically.
By requiring the user to describe the test in plain English to an AI chatbot.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Creating a test starts with recording the actions taken in the AUT browser; each action becomes a step in the test procedure. No manual scripting, document import, or chatbot description is required for this basic flow.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the main purpose of Testim's Smart Locators?

options.text: To speed up test recording by skipping element analysis entirely.
To uniquely identify an element using many weighted attributes, so the test keeps finding it even after minor UI changes.
To automatically translate the test into another programming language.
To generate documentation for every step in the test.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's about resilience to change, not speed or translation.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Smart Locators analyze potentially hundreds of attributes per element, weight them, and adapt across runs — so if some attributes change, the element can still be found using others. This is what keeps tests from breaking on every small UI tweak.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does each box in the recorded test procedure represent?

options.text: A step, with an icon indicating the type of action performed.
A folder in the Test Library.
A user account used during the recording.

practiceQuiz.hint: Each box maps 1:1 to a recorded action.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Each box represents a step in the test procedure, with an icon in the upper-left corner indicating the type of action (click, enter text, scroll, etc.). It is not a separate test, a folder, or a user account.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After running a saved test, what does Testim surface to help you diagnose a failure?

options.text: Only a generic pass/fail flag for the entire test, with no further detail.
The per-step pass/fail result along with the reason a step failed.
A full video of a human manually re-running the test.
Nothing — results must be inspected by re-running the test manually.

practiceQuiz.hint: Diagnosis works at the step level, not just the whole-test level.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Testim reports pass/fail per step and per test and surfaces the failure reason (e.g. element not found, element not visible), letting you diagnose without a full manual re-run.

quickRecap.value: Actions taken in the AUT browser become editable steps — no code required.
Hundreds of weighted attributes per element; Testim adapts across runs instead of breaking on minor changes.
Tests live in the project's Test Library — foldered, labeled, and re-runnable.
Pass/fail per step, with the failure reason surfaced for fast diagnosis.
